basis_statement: Visibility partition keys are required only for cache scopes that can otherwise replay broader list or workspace slices across narrower customer- or role-bounded views.

notes: Low-noise frames remain route-bound and do not publish a separate visibility partition key.
Workspace visibility partitions separate staff, customer-safe, and narrower task-slice variants even when route and object stay stable.
Inbox partitions freeze which list slice is visible, not just which route is mounted.
Portal partitions stay customer-safe and must distinguish invite, history, and masking posture slices.
Customer request-list partitions protect customer-safe list slices from broader support variants.
Governance snapshots are tenant-governed and therefore do not use customer-visibility partitions.
Governance policy snapshots keep artifact visibility out of the cache identity envelope.
Principal-access views are governance-scoped rather than customer-visibility-scoped.
Role-template matrices do not publish per-customer visibility partitions.
Native primary scenes bind legality through route, object, access, and masking instead of a separate list-slice partition.
Native secondary windows rely on preview subject binding rather than a visibility partition key.

source_lineage.rationale: Names the scope classes that must carry a visibility cache partition key and the governance classes that must not.
